source: Erickson Schultz Crone 2025 Ecosphere doi:10.1002/ecs2.70259; Figshare source file Milkweed_dat_with_coords_DEC2024.csv
selection: Three largest 2022 source species by number of counted plants (A. curassavica, A. fascicularis, A. speciosa), before any additional plant-species cutoff tuning; species pair tests are fully posthoc.
question: Are native-exotic stage composition contrasts actually botanical species effects? Compare native-vs-native A. fascicularis/A. speciosa, and exotic A.curassavica vs each native species.
statistic: Exotic/native or first/second species Mantel-Haenszel OR of later larvae (instars 4+5) to eggs across identical survey route x month when both species are recorded and each has >=1 egg/larva stage event.
uncertainty: 4999 nonparametric route-block bootstrap resampling all 15 sampled routes, seed 20261008; report undefined draws.
season_windows: Winter Jan-Mar; spring Apr-Jun; summer Jul-Sep; fall Oct-Dec, unchanged from stage protocol
negative_control: Native-vs-native species pair tests whether binary nativeness itself provides a useful explanation
limitations: Selection follows prior observed 2022 stage contrast, so no confirmatory p-values.
Species pair changes the retained route/month strata; cannot attribute differences strictly to species physiology.
Counts are eggs and older larvae measured cross-sectionally, NOT survival or fitness.
Route and month adjustment does not hold observer/detection, patch position, architecture, management or plant life stage constant.
This reanalyses already published field data; no external replication, and no main GEB changes.
